reference_notes: Philip's canonical ADR-0037 example (2026-07-27). Cut-string, half-open-riser walnut staircase. Used as the reference standard for what Claude Sonnet vision must produce for a similar unseen image. Source image: https://ik.imagekit.io/5vv5pw26q/ChatGPT%20Image%20Jul%2023,%202026,%2004_10_51%20PM.png?updatedAt=1784797870414
quality_bar: Every future vision extraction on any staircase image is compared to this. If the model produces flat descriptive tags instead of reasoning, the extraction is rejected and the system prompt is tuned.

recognition_features: solid timber treads extending over string

function_reasoning: provides child safety by reducing large open gaps
prevents head entrapment risk compared with fully open risers
adds visual solidity while maintaining open staircase appearance
structural_reasoning: extra thick timber treads used to compensate for reduced support from open riser construction
treads provide additional stiffness and strength
treads are screw-fixed from the rear into the tread construction
riser does not act as a full structural support member

not_present: no angle support blocks between tread and riser
no traditional housed string wedge system visible
joinery_details.reason: open rear construction leaves the underside visible, creating a furniture-style staircase appearance
